chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman, from Musa ibn Qadim, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The completion of the visit to the sick person is that you place your hand upon his forearm and hasten your departure from his presence, for the visit of the foolish is more burdensome upon the sick person than his own pain.

key_terms.الذراع: Forearm — the physical gesture of placing the hand here signifies care and connection
key_terms.العيادة: Visiting the sick (iyada) — a recommended act in Islam with specific etiquette
key_terms.النوكى: The foolish/ignorant ones (al-nawka) — those who visit without consideration of the patient's condition
key_terms.الوجع: Pain/suffering — the patient's existing physical ailment

ai.seo_question: What is the proper etiquette for visiting the sick according to Imam Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides a nuanced etiquette for visiting the sick: a proper visit involves a brief, warm physical gesture of placing one's hand on the patient's forearm, followed by a prompt departure. The teaching cautions against overstaying, noting that an inconsiderate or lengthy visit by an ignorant visitor imposes additional suffering upon the patient beyond their illness. This reflects the Islamic principle that care for others must be guided by awareness of their needs rather than one's own desire to express concern.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Suleyman, from Musa Bin Qadim, from a man, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The completion of the visitation to the sick is that you place your hand upon his forearm and hasten the arising from his presence, for the foolish visitation is difficult upon the patient due to his pain’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn Sulayman from Musa ibn Qadim from a man who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
visiting of a patient is complete upon placing your hand over his arm (praying) and standing up quickly to leave; an unwise visiting of a patient is harder for him than the pain due to illness.”
